newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rains disrupt south Germany farm work, north dry.
newsitem.headline: Rains disrupt south Germany farm work, north dry.

text.p: Rains disrupted farm work in Germany's south while northern regions stayed mostly dry, the DWD meteorological office said in a weekly report.
"Most maize and more than half of the sugar beet crop has been harvested and winter grain crops in the ground are developing normally," a DWD source said.
Sugar beet is temporarily stored on the fields and covered before it is driven to factories in the beet campaign, which lasts at least into December.
DWD said temperatures were dropping fast, but winter rapeseed had developed a little too quickly during recent warm spells, which could lessen its resistance to winter frosts.
DWD forecast changeable weather and rains in the south and the east in the week to November 20.
Maximum daytime temperatures in the period should be five degrees and some night frosts should set in.
Maximum temperatures in the week to November 13 were 10 to 16 degrees.
